summary: On node1 (RHEL 10), installed nginx + openssl, configured nginx to serve HTTPS on port 8443 using a self-signed certificate stored under /etc/pki/tls/rotating, and set up a systemd oneshot service (cert-renew.service) fired every 5 minutes by cert-renew.timer to regenerate the certificate and reload nginx (zero-downtime reload, no restart). Verified automatic renewal, continuous request availability across a live cert swap, and that the automation and TLS endpoint both recover intact across a full node restart.
actions_performed: Installed nginx and openssl on node1 via dnf
Created /usr/local/bin/renew-cert.sh which generates a self-signed cert (1-day validity, SAN=node IP) and installs it atomically into /etc/pki/tls/rotating, then runs systemctl reload nginx
Configured /etc/nginx/conf.d/rotating-tls.conf to listen on 8443 (ssl) using the rotating cert/key paths
Enabled and started nginx; verified HTTPS on 8443 via curl and openssl s_client
Created cert-renew.service (oneshot, Requires=nginx.service) and cert-renew.timer (OnUnitActiveSec=5min, Persistent=true); enabled the timer
Ran a 60-second continuous curl probe loop spanning a live automatic renewal cycle to prove zero downtime during the cert swap/reload
Captured pre-restart baseline: boot_id, nginx/timer active+enabled state, live TLS certificate serial
Issued systemctl reboot on node1 in the background so the ack returned before disconnect, then polled until the node reconnected
Verified a new boot_id and new uptime-since after the restart, confirming nginx and cert-renew.timer auto-started and are active without manual intervention
Confirmed HTTPS still served content and observed a further automatic certificate renewal (new serial) occurring after the restart, proving the automation persists

evidence.requirement: HTTPS served on port 8443 with a valid certificate
evidence.summary: nginx enabled+active, listening on 0.0.0.0:8443 and [::]:8443; curl over TLS returns 'ok' and openssl s_client shows the served certificate serial/dates

cert-renew.timer installed and enabled (OnUnitActiveSec=5min); journalctl shows cert-renew.service fired on schedule and produced a new certificate serial (2605D6... -> 03F916DF...) without manual action

evidence.requirement: Service keeps answering requests while picking up the new certificate (no downtime during rotation)
evidence.summary: 60 consecutive HTTPS probes taken across the exact window the timer fired and nginx reloaded all returned HTTP 200; post-swap TLS handshake serial confirms the new cert was actually served
Captured boot_id d9f8550d-5cb3-4929-9e62-a388df86bcf6, uptime-since, enabled state of nginx and cert-renew.timer, and the live-served cert serial before restart

evidence.requirement: Single-node restart executed safely with returned acknowledgement
evidence.summary: systemctl reboot issued in background; command acknowledged (rc=0) before the node disconnected

evidence.requirement: Node restart proven via changed boot identity
evidence.summary: Connection timed out while rebooting (node down), then reconnected with boot_id 88e63dc5-dc1f-40e1-a831-5ec0540f54f7 and new uptime-since 2026-09-29 10:13:20, differing from the pre-restart boot_id

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of TLS service and renewal automation, including continued automatic renewal
evidence.summary: nginx and cert-renew.timer both active immediately after reboot; HTTPS on 8443 still serves; a further scheduled renewal fired post-reboot producing a new cert serial (12807F1E...) while nginx kept serving 'ok'
